parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no birth-sex facility rule, and visitor-facing remedies that demonstrably work: a national court awarded damages against a service that excluded a trans woman, an apprehended-violence order was granted against a targeted harasser, and a current national hate-crime law covers gender identity with seven-year penalties. Detention standards (one state) direct placement by lived gender under an active oversight act. No targeting of trans visitors is documented. Offsets: organised exclusionary campaigns are recorded, facilities/records access are contested friction points, state discrimination coverage is patchy (two states cover neither ground), one state restricted youth care amid legal back-and-forth, prosecution data under the new hate-crime law is absent, and document-marker practice rests on dated sources. These are tier-3 frictions and open questions, not tier-1 exposures. Reduced-to-low risk; slightly below the 0.85 anchor because protections are partly untested and subnational coverage uneven.
